anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

choices.term: ἐν ᾗ ὁ Σταυρὸς σφῦρα καὶ ἄκμων ἡ Ἀνάστασις
choices.english: on which the Cross was the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil
choices.why: σφῦρα is a hammer and ἄκμων an anvil: the trumpet is pictured as metal worked at a forge.
rejected: where the Cross is a flint and the Resurrection an anvil

choices.why: πυρόω of metal is to fire or temper it, which fits the forge image of the next clause.

choices.english: has gathered this spiritual assembly for us
choices.why: θέατρον here is the gathered congregation, not a building; ἡμῖν is 'for us'.
rejected: has gathered us into this spiritual theater

choices.term: μνῆμα φθορᾶς <μὲν> ἐλεύθερον, ἀφθαρσίας δὲ πρόξενον
choices.english: a grave free of corruption that yet brings about incorruption
choices.why: ἐλεύθερον with the genitive is 'free of'; πρόξενος is one who procures or brings something about. The μὲν ... δὲ contrast is kept with 'yet'.
rejected: a memorial of corruption yet a herald of incorruption

choices.english: a bridal chamber that laid the bridegroom to sleep for three days
choices.why: κοιμάω is to put to sleep, the Fathers' word for death before rising; τριήμερον gives the three days.
rejected: a bridal bed that buried the bridegroom

choices.term: νεκρὸν μὲν γὰρ αὐτὸν τὸ σῶμα βοᾷ, τὸ δὲ θαῦμα θεόν
choices.english: his body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle that he is God
choices.why: βοᾷ governs the whole series of pairs; each pair sets a sign of death against a sign of Godhead.
rejected: the dead women and their tears, God the angels' words

pass_a_gloss: A trumpet (σάλπιγξ) for us, sacred and royal, this spiritual theatre-gathering (θέατρον) has drawn together (συγκροτέω): a trumpet which Bethlehem filled and Zion fired (πυρόω), in which the Cross [is] hammer (σφῦρα) and anvil (ἄκμων) the Resurrection. Of which I know not how I may speak out the beauty, how express the light, how make known the joy in it, how relate the kingdom in it. With what hand shall I handle (ψηλαφάω) it? With what words shall I greet (ἀσπάζομαι) a tomb begetting life, a grave (μνῆμα) on the one hand free of corruption (φθορά), on the other procurer (πρόξενος) of incorruption (ἀφθαρσία), a three-day bridal chamber (παστάς) having put the bridegroom to sleep (κοιμάω), a bridal room (νυμφών) having raised the bride undefiled after marriage? Dead [it shows him], the guarded burial place (θήκη), and God, the shaken earth; for dead the body shouts (βοάω) him, but the wonder God; dead the burial, God the resurrection; dead also the tears of the women, and God the words of the angels. As dead Joseph buried (κηδεύω) him, but the one buried as [continues in the next section: a man]
pass_b_english: A sacred and royal trumpet has gathered this spiritual assembly for us: a trumpet that Bethlehem filled and Zion tempered in fire, on which the Cross was the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil. I do not know how to tell its beauty, how to describe its light, how to make known the joy within it, how to recount the kingdom within it. With what hand shall I touch it?

With what words shall I greet a tomb that gives birth to life, a grave free of corruption that yet brings about incorruption, a bridal chamber that laid the bridegroom to sleep for three days, a bridal room that raised the bride incorrupt after the marriage? The guarded tomb declares him dead, and the quaking earth declares him God. For his body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle that he is God; the burial, that he is dead, the resurrection, that he is God; the tears of the women, that he is dead, and the words of the angels, that he is God. Joseph buried him as one dead, but he who was buried as a man…
source_text:
Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (homilia 4) (e cod. Sinaitico gr. 492)
Τοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πάσχα
1 Σάλπιγξ ἡμῖν ἱερὰ καὶ βασιλικὴ τὸ πνευματικὸν τοῦτο συνεκρότησεν
θέατρον, σάλπιγξ ἣν ἐπλήρωσεν Βηθλεὲμ καὶ ἡ Σιὼν ἐπύρωσεν, ἐν ᾗ ὁ Σταυρὸς
σφῦρα καὶ ἄκμων ἡ Ἀνάστασις. Ἧς οὐκ οἶδα πῶς ἐξείπω τὸ κάλλος, πῶς ἐκφράσω τὸ
φῶς, πῶς μηνύσω τὴν ἐν αὐτῷ χαράν, πῶς τὴν ἐν αὐτῇ βασιλείαν διηγήσωμαι. Ποίᾳ
δὲ αὐτὴν ψηλαφήσω χειρί;
2 Ποίοις λόγοις ἀσπάσομαι τάφον γεννῶντα ζωήν, μνῆμα φθορᾶς <μὲν>
ἐλεύθερον, ἀφθαρσίας δὲ πρόξενον, παστάδα τριή μερον τὸν νυμφίον κοιμήσασαν,
νυμφῶνα τὴν νύμφην ἄφθορον μετὰ γάμον ἐγείραντα; Νεκρὸν ἡ θήκη φυλαττομένη
καὶ θεὸν ἡ γῆ σαλευομένη· νεκρὸν μὲν γὰρ αὐτὸν τὸ σῶμα βοᾷ, τὸ δὲ θαῦμα θεόν·
νεκρὸν ἡ ταφή, θεὸν ἡ ἀνάστασις· νεκρὸν τῶν γυναικῶν καὶ τὰ δάκρυα, καὶ θεὸν
τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰ ῥήματα. Ὡς νεκρὸν αὐτὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἐκήδευσεν, ἀλλ' ὁ κηδευθεὶς ὡς
